sandhi.note: Visarga after i, before a vowel, is sounded as r.

mantras.anvaya_en: Subject and verb: a speaker label.

comm.t: Medhas, still speaking to King Suratha and the merchant Samādhi, begins the second story: the Goddess’s war with Mahiṣāsura and his armies. This uvāca opens the middle carita (Madhyama Carita), which runs from chapter 2 to chapter 4.

In the Gita Press pāṭha the middle carita has its own viniyoga and dhyāna, recited before this mantra: Viṣṇu is named its ṛṣi, Mahālakṣmī its deity, uṣṇik its metre, Śākambharī its śakti and Durgā its bīja. This is liturgical tradition, not part of the Purāṇa. The bījas ॐ ह्रीं that open the mantra in recitation belong to the same pāṭha.

words.en: of the gods and asuras, between gods and asuras
words.g: n. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies युद्धम्
√भू (bhvādi, 1P ‘to be, become’), luṅ (aorist), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada

√पॄ + क्त (‘filled’), n. acc. sg.; qualifies अब्दशतम्
n. acc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); accusative of duration of time
indeclinable (adverb of time)
m. loc. sg. of महिष, ‘buffalo’, here the asura’s name; locative absolute (सति understood)
m. gen. pl. of असुर; depends on अधिपे
m. loc. sg. of अधिप (अधि + √पा ‘to protect’ + क); predicate in the locative absolute

sandhi.note: a + a → ā: देव + असुर → देवासुर.
Final t becomes d before the voiced y. The m of युद्धम् becomes anusvāra before the p of पूर्णम् (मोऽनुस्वारः, 8.3.23).

Final e absorbs the initial a (avagraha). Even with this elision the pāda महिषेऽसुराणामधिपे counts nine syllables, one more than the eight of an anuṣṭubh pāda: it is hypermetric, as in every witness (see the metre notes).

samasa.sense: the war between the gods and the asuras
samasa.alt: It can also be taken as a samāhāra dvandva (neuter singular) in loose apposition to युद्धम्. The regular adjective of relation would be दैवासुर (with vṛddhi); the Purāṇas use the bare dvandva in the stock phrase देवासुरं युद्धम्, and the attributive reading fits the agreement with युद्धम्.

samasa.sense: Indra, breaker of the enemies’ forts; the first member takes the augment m (पुरम्-दर)

morph.note: Locative absolute (sati saptamī): महिषे असुराणाम् अधिपे (सति), ‘Mahiṣa being lord of the asuras’; the second, पुरन्दरे देवानाम् (अधिपे सति), shares the same predicate.
Accusative of duration: the time over which something lasts stands in the accusative, ‘for a hundred years’.
Root aorist of √भू with augment a-, ‘there was’; as in 1.4, used for narrative past.

mantras.anvaya: पुरा असुराणाम् अधिपे महिषे, देवानां च (अधिपे) पुरन्दरे (सति), पूर्णम् अब्दशतं देवासुरं युद्धम् अभूत्।
mantras.anvaya_en: The main clause (देवासुरं युद्धम् अभूत्, with पूर्णम् अब्दशतम् for its length) comes first; two locative absolutes name the leaders on each side.
mantras.lit: Long ago there was a war of gods and asuras for a full hundred years, Mahiṣa being lord of the asuras and Purandara of the gods.
mantras.tr: Long ago the gods and the asuras fought for a full hundred years, when Mahiṣa was lord of the asuras and Indra lord of the gods.
mantras.tr_note: Purandara is rendered by the familiar name Indra in tr.

comm.t: The second story opens like the first, with a time and a conflict: a hundred-year war, with Mahiṣa leading the asuras and Indra the gods. The first pāda of the second line is one syllable too long (nine, not eight) in every witness; the text is left as it is.

Mahiṣa means ‘buffalo’; the asura’s buffalo form appears in chapter 3, where he fights the Goddess in that shape and in others. The tradition calls the Goddess of this carita Mahiṣāsuramardinī, ‘crusher of the buffalo-asura’.

sandhi.note: a + a → ā (तत्रासुरैः). After ai the visarga (as रु) is sounded r before the voiced m and d.
-aḥ before a: the visarga becomes u, a + u → o, and the following a is elided (avagraha). Then the final t of अभूत् becomes the nasal n before the m of महिषासुरः.

samasa.sense: mighty, heroic asuras; महत् becomes महा- in the compound

samasa.literal: the asura who is Mahiṣa (the buffalo)
samasa.alt: Also explained as a karmadhāraya with an elided middle member (महिषरूपः असुरः, ‘the asura in buffalo form’). Since महिष is his name in 2.2, the simple appositional reading fits.

morph.note: Past passive participle used as a finite verb: ‘(was) defeated’. With परा, √जि means ‘to defeat’ (and takes ātmanepada when finite).
Absolutive (क्त्वा) of √जि: ‘having conquered’. It shares its agent with the main verb: Mahiṣāsura conquered, then became Indra.

mantras.anvaya: तत्र महावीर्यैः असुरैः देवसैन्यं पराजितम्। सकलान् देवान् जित्वा च महिषासुरः इन्द्रः अभूत्।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two sentences: a passive one (देवसैन्यं पराजितम्, agent in the instrumental) and an active one with an absolutive (जित्वा … महिषासुरः इन्द्रः अभूत्).
mantras.lit: There the army of the gods was defeated by the asuras of great valour; and having conquered all the gods, Mahiṣāsura became Indra.
mantras.tr: In that war the mighty asuras routed the army of the gods; and having conquered every god, Mahiṣāsura made himself Indra.
mantras.tr_note: ‘Made himself Indra’ renders इन्द्रः अभूत् ‘became Indra’, i.e. took Indra’s place as king of heaven.

comm.t: The war ends in the gods’ defeat, and Mahiṣa takes Indra’s place. ‘Indra’ here is an office: lordship over heaven, which the victor seizes.

The gods’ complaint (2.6) spells out what the usurpation means: Mahiṣa occupies the offices (अधिकारान्) of the Sun, Fire, Wind, Moon, Yama and Varuṇa as well as Indra’s. Cosmic functions in the Purāṇas are posts held by gods, and here they have been taken over by a single asura.

words.en: the Lord (Śiva) and the Garuḍa-bannered one (Viṣṇu)
words.g: m. nom. dual; compound (see Samāsa); subject of the relative clause (स्थितौ ‘were’ understood)

sandhi.note: -āḥ before a voiced sound: the visarga (as रु) becomes y, and the y is dropped before a consonant, leaving -ā.

samasa.literal: he whose source is the lotus
samasa.sense: Brahmā, born from the lotus of Viṣṇu’s navel
Śiva and Viṣṇu; the dual counts the two members

samasa.literal: he who has Garuḍa on his banner

morph.note: Absolutive of पुरस् + √कृ: पुरस् is treated as a verbal prefix (gati), so the absolutive takes -य (ल्यप्), with t inserted after the short ṛ: पुरस्कृ-त्-य. ‘Having put in front’: the gods go with Brahmā leading them.
Past participle of √गम् standing for a finite verb: ‘(they) went’.

mantras.anvaya: ततः पराजिताः देवाः पद्मयोनिं प्रजापतिं पुरस्कृत्य, यत्र ईशगरुडध्वजौ (स्थितौ), तत्र गताः।
mantras.anvaya_en: Main clause देवाः … गताः, with an absolutive phrase (पुरस्कृत्य) and a relative clause of place (यत्र …) answered by तत्र.
mantras.lit: Then the defeated gods, placing at their head the lotus-born Prajāpati, went there where the Lord and the Garuḍa-bannered one were.
mantras.tr: Then the defeated gods, with Brahmā the lotus-born creator at their head, went to where Śiva and Viṣṇu were.
mantras.tr_note: ईश and गरुडध्वज are rendered by the names Śiva and Viṣṇu; ‘were’ is supplied.

comm.t: The gods go to the two great gods with Brahmā at their head. This is the usual Purāṇic pattern: when the lesser gods are defeated, they seek the higher powers.

All three gods of the trimūrti are present. The Goddess who appears will come from their tejas first (2.10) and then from that of all the others (2.11). In the first carita Brahmā alone praised her; here all the gods together bring her forth.

words.g: indeclinable; compound (see Samāsa), used adverbially
pronoun तद्, m. gen. dual; the hearers of कथयामासुः (genitive for dative)

words.en: likewise, and in the same way
words.g: indeclinable (तद् + taddhita वति ‘like that’)
n. acc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); object of कथयामासुः
m. nom. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); subject
√कथ् (curādi, 10 ‘to tell’), liṭ (periphrastic perfect), prathama-puruṣa bahuvacana, parasmaipada

words.en: the full account of the gods’ humiliation
words.g: m. acc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); second object of कथयामासुः

sandhi.note: Visarga before t becomes s (तयोस्तद्वत्); final t before the nasal m becomes n (तद्वन्महिषासुर).
After u the visarga (as रु) is sounded r before the voiced d. Inside the compound, देव + अभिभव → देवाभिभव (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः, 6.1.101).

samasa.alt: It could also be read as an adjective (‘as it had happened’) qualifying महिषासुरचेष्टितम्; the adverbial avyayībhāva is the usual use of यथावृत्तम्.

samasa.literal: those whose count is three tens
samasa.sense: the gods, ‘the Thirty’ (a round number for the thirty-three gods)
samasa.alt: A traditional etymology instead takes दशा ‘stage of life’: the gods know only three stages and never grow old. The numerical sense is the usual one.

samasa.vigraha: देवानाम् अभिभवः देवाभिभवः; तस्य विस्तरः, तम्
samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (outer), containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (देवाभिभव)
samasa.literal: the detail of the overpowering of the gods
samasa.sense: the whole story of how the gods were humbled

morph.note: Periphrastic perfect: a derived (here curādi) stem कथय- cannot reduplicate, so it takes -आम् and the perfect of √अस् (आसुः, 3rd pl.): कथयाम् + आसुः.
तद् + the taddhita वति ‘like’: ‘in that way, likewise’. Here it links the two objects: Mahiṣāsura’s doings and, likewise, the gods’ defeat.

mantras.anvaya: त्रिदशाः तयोः महिषासुरचेष्टितं तद्वत् देवाभिभवविस्तरं (च) यथावृत्तं कथयामासुः।
mantras.anvaya_en: Subject (त्रिदशाः), hearers in the genitive (तयोः), two objects joined by तद्वत्, the manner (यथावृत्तम्), and the verb.
mantras.lit: The Thirty related to those two, just as it happened, the doings of Mahiṣāsura and likewise the full account of the gods’ humiliation.
mantras.tr: The gods told the two of them everything Mahiṣāsura had done, exactly as it happened, and the whole story of their own defeat.

comm.t: The gods report to Śiva and Viṣṇu. The next three verses (2.6–8) give their report in their own words.

The gods here are called ‘the Thirty’ (त्रिदशाः), a common name of the gods in epic and Purāṇic Sanskrit. The text gives Mahiṣa’s offence twice: first in the narrator’s summary (2.3), then from the gods’ side as humiliation (अभिभव).
